evidence.observation: 架空菓庵 is a fictional traditional wagashi shop; its name is four kanji.
Seasonal jō-namagashi and dorayaki with tsubu-an cooked every morning, wrapped one at a time at a small shopfront (小さな店頭).
After the faithful v2 build the owner asked for a more premium feel and originality than a plain left-right split hero and two equal product cards.
evidence.source_label: Owner instruction in the Issue #117 session, 2026-10-24

references.observed_principle: 複数の縦長ページが、和文縦組み・小さな説明文・茶器の写真・余白の繰り返しを使う。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a short Japanese heading set vertically beside horizontal facts changes the reading axis; no page, image or copy is reused.

references.observed_principle: 広い淡色の余白の中、ケーキ写真を島のように置き、右端に日本語縦書きを入れる。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: vertical Japanese type can sit beside product imagery in pale open space; the cake site's composition is not reused.

references.observed_principle: 白い面と薄い緑、中央の縦方向の日本語説明、下部の茶葉・茶碗と小さな説明を整列した構図。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle of a calm section rhythm (that brand avoids a premium identity, so it is not cited for luxury or for its animation).

references.observed_principle: 白い画面の上端に小さなタイプロゴ、中心に横長の店内写真、その下に非常に細い情報の区切り。
references.transferable_idea: Only the principle: a small type logo above one quiet image block and a very thin information divider keep a page calm.

decisions.choice: An asymmetric hero, not a left-right split: the approved dorayaki crop in a framed window on the left with wide paper ground around it, the four-kanji name as one tall vertical column on the right, and a steep size drop to a small header and a quiet text link.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for more than a plain split and two equal cards; a framed image plus a vertical name gives one clear focal pair instead of two halves.

decisions.choice: The name alone is set vertically in a large refined Mincho; nav, section headings, the description line and every fact stay horizontal at reading size.
decisions.rationale: A four-kanji name reads well top to bottom, while hours, address and phone must stay horizontal to be read; only the name changes axis.

decisions.choice: Kinari ground over most of the page, sumi text, and a deep azuki tone used only as one thin rule under the active nav and a hairline above the ledger; no filled button and no decorative mark.
decisions.rationale: The one accent takes its hue from the shop's own tsubu-an, and keeping it to hairlines answers the owner's request for a quieter, more premium page.

decisions.choice: Two approved concept crops of clearly different sizes, never a row of equal cards: the dorayaki large in the hero frame, the seasonal namagashi small beside the description line; no dots or other invented marks.
decisions.rationale: The description names exactly two things, seasonal namagashi and tsubu-an dorayaki, so two images of unequal weight carry it without filler.

decisions.choice: Each section has a different lead: the framed image and vertical name in the hero, one verbatim description sentence set large in the middle, a narrow factual ledger last.
decisions.rationale: The description moves from the morning's tsubu-an to wrapping each sweet at the small shopfront, so the middle section is led by words, not a second image row.

decisions.choice: A thin horizontal header with the name and two anchors to the details and the shop information; nothing about ordering or reservations.
decisions.rationale: The fixture offers no ordering, so the header only reaches verified content and stays small beside a large vertical name.

decisions.choice: On a phone the name turns horizontal and large above the hero image; the dot mark, the description sentence and the ledger follow in one column.
decisions.rationale: A vertical name in a 390px column would crowd the image, and the whole four-kanji name has to be read before anything decorative.

decisions.choice: The comp shows true vertical type; the build either gets the writing-mode capability approved (DEV-083) or keeps the name horizontal. A one-character-wide box is not used to fake vertical type.
decisions.rationale: Real vertical setting is outside the current page CSS allowlist, and a stacked one-character box breaks spacing and polish, so the build must not pretend it is the same.
